newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening higher after data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening higher after data.

text.p: U.S. stocks are expected to open higher on Thursday after November consumer price (CPI) and retail sales data pointed to a slowly growing economy with little inflationary pressure, analysts said.

"Core and nominal CPI were in line, so there are no problems there. Retail sales were clearly the story here and were materially weaker than expected. This advances the cause that this economy is decelerating and (Fed) Chairman Alan Greenspan has no need to tighten at next week's meeting," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.

The consumer price index rose 0.3 percent, after rising by the same amount in October. Retail sales fell 0.4 percent in November to a seasonally adjusted $206.1 billion after a revised 0.3 percent rise in October.
